newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen to build 550 mln DM steel mill.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen to build 550 mln DM steel mill.

text.p: German steelmaker Thyssen Stahl AG said on Friday that it would build a thin slab casting mill at a cost of 550 million marks ($366.2 million) in the German city of Duisburg.

The mill, the first of its type in Germany, would have capacity of 1.2 million tonnes per year. It would work together with Thyssen Stahl's two existing hot steel rolling mills in Duisburg and employ 170 workers. ($ = 1.501 German Marks)

The investment will be the main project in an 881 million mark programme at Thyssen Stahl, which will concentrate on flat steel production under a restructuring plan approved on Friday by the supervisory board of parent Thyssen AG.

The new mill will allow Thyssen to obtain savings in production of hot slabs by reducing the width of the poured slab to 60 mm from 250 mm typical for the large hot-rolling mills in its integrated steel works.
The thin-slab will then be sent through a warming oven and rolling train, where it will be pounded to a thickness of one millimetre.
The thin-slab casting and rolling facility, consisting of two strands side-by-side, will be integrated into Thyssen's basic oxygen steel mill at its Duisburg-Brockhausen facility.
A Thyssen Stahl spokesman said the new mill could begin operating by the beginning of 1999.
He said the company was still negotiating with several steel plant manufacturers but that it had not decided on the final contract to build the mill.

While there are few companies in the world that come into question, several that build this kind of steel mill include Germany's SMS Schloemann Siemag AG, which developed the first thin-slab casting mill for Nucor Steel of the United States.
Other companies include VA Stahl of Austria and Mannesmann Demag, also of Germany.
